14.1:
Approach: A case routing pipeline starts with a queue (Group of type Queue) that acts as a shared work pool, then an assignment rule decides which cases land in that queue. Build it declaratively in Setup, then verify the wiring with SOQL.

Setup:

  1. Setup â†’ Queues â†’ New Queue: label Premium Support, assign Case, add group and user members (the agents who can work and run reports on the queue).
  2. Setup â†’ Case Assignment Rules â†’ New: name it Premium Routing.
  3. Add an entry (entries are evaluated top to bottom, first match wins): criteria Priority = High and Origin = Web â†’ assign to the Premium Support queue. Add a catch-all entry for everyone else to Tier 1.
  4. Keep the rule in the right sort order (sort accordingly) and check Active.
apex
// 1) Verify the queue exists with the right type
SELECT Id, Name, DeveloperName, Type, CreatedDate
FROM Group
WHERE Type = 'Queue'
ORDER BY Name
apex
// 2) Verify the assignment rule is active for Case
SELECT Id, Name, SobjectType, IsActive
FROM AssignmentRule
WHERE SobjectType = 'Case'
apex
// 3) See how many open cases are sitting in each queue
Map<Id, Integer> perQueue = new Map<Id, Integer>();
for (AggregateResult ar : [
  SELECT OwnerId, COUNT(Id) n
  FROM Case
  WHERE OwnerId IN (
    SELECT Id FROM Group WHERE Type = 'Queue'
  )
  GROUP BY OwnerId
]) {
  perQueue.put((Id) ar.get('OwnerId'), (Integer) ar.get('n'));
}
System.debug('Cases per queue: ' + perQueue);

Expected result: The query in step 1 returns the queue with Type = 'Queue', step 2 returns IsActive = true, and new cases that match the entry criteria are owned by the queue instead of an individual user. The owner picklist shows the queue name and case reports can group by Owner (queue).

Common mistakes:

  • Forgetting that rule entries are evaluated in order â€” an earlier broad entry swallows cases intended for a later specific one.
  • Deploying/running with IsActive = false so no cases ever route.
  • Expecting assignment rules to fire when a case is inserted from Apex or Flow. Assignment rules run on UI/API create; direct Apex inserts do not trigger them (leave OwnerId null and insert through the UI/API path instead).
  • Adding a queue but not adding member users, so nobody can see or claim the work.
  • Editing the active rule on top of test data â€” rule history only applies to new inserts, not existing cases.
14.2:
Approach: Escalation rules are time-based Case automations. They evaluate how long a case has been open since it was created or last updated and, when the case is saved, apply the matching rule entry actions: reassign the case, change status/priority, run an outbound email template, or notify an assigned user. Critically they run when a case is saved, not as a background job in the middle of the night.

Setup:

  1. Setup â†’ Escalation Rules â†’ New VIP Escalation and activate it.

  2. In the rule detail, add a rule entry:

    • Criteria: Priority = High, Status != Closed.
    • Time based: After 2 hours from case creation, using Business hours only (choose a Business Hours record so weekend hours do not count).
    • Actions: reassign to the Tier 2 queue, set Status = Escalated, set Priority = Critical.
  3. Create a Business Hours record (Setup â†’ Business Hours) for your support hours and keep it in the entry so the clock only ticks during working time.
apex
// Verify escalation rules are active
SELECT Id, Name, SobjectType, IsActive, LastModifiedDate
FROM EscalationRule
WHERE SobjectType = 'Case'
ORDER BY LastModifiedDate DESC
apex
// Verify the business hours used by the rule
SELECT Id, Name, IsActive, IsDefault
FROM BusinessHours
apex
// If a true background timer is required, schedule a batch that flags
// cases whose age exceeds the threshold (Apex alternative to escalation rules)
public class CaseAgeEscalator implements Schedulable {
  public void execute(SchedulableContext ctx) {
    Database.executeBatch(new CaseAgeEscalatorBatch(), 200);
  }
  public class CaseAgeEscalatorBatch implements Database.Batchable<SObject> {
    public Database.QueryLocator start(Database.BatchableContext bc) {
      return Database.getQueryLocator([
        SELECT Id, CaseNumber, OwnerId
        FROM Case
        WHERE Status != 'Closed'
          AND CreatedDate < LAST_N_DAYS:1
      ]);
    }
    public void execute(Database.BatchableContext bc, List<SObject> scope) {
      for (SObject s : scope) {
        Case c = (Case) s;
        System.debug('Escalating stale case ' + c.CaseNumber + ' for review');
      }
    }
    public void finish(Database.BatchableContext bc) {
      System.debug('Case age escalation finished');
    }
  }
}

Expected result: When an agent (or integration) saves a high-priority case that is older than the threshold, the case is automatically reassigned to the Tier 2 queue and flagged as escalated. The EscalationRule query shows an active rule, and the Business Hours query confirms working-time configuration.

Common mistakes:

  • Assuming escalation runs at the exact time the clock ticks â€” it only applies on the next case save. Use a scheduled batch (as above) if you need a true background check.
  • Configuring calendar hours when you want business hours, which makes weeknights/weekends count against the SLA.
  • Removing the Time Based checkbox from an entry so a threshold is never evaluated.
  • Building the action but not activating the rule entry/rule (actions are ignored for inactive rules).
  • Changing an entry after cases already match it â€” the new criteria apply to future evaluations, not retroactively.
14.3:
Approach: Omni-Channel pushes work to agents in real time based on presence and routing configuration. Case work items come from the standard Case channel, agents report presence through presence statuses, and routing configs decide which work items each agent sees. This is the readiness layer that makes queues feel like a live call center for case work.

Setup:

  1. Enable Omni-Channel: Setup â†’ Omni-Channel Settings â†’ enable.
  2. Service Channels: the Case channel is created for you; verify it is enabled.
  3. Presence Statuses: create Available, Working on Cases, Offline in Setup â†’ Omni-Channel â†’ Presence Statuses and enable them so agents can authenticate their state.
  4. Routing Config: Setup â†’ Omni-Channel â†’ Routing Configurations â†’ Case Routing: set Routing Order 1, enable skills-based routing if you want named skills, and keep it active.
  5. Assign the routing config to the users or queues that should receive work.
apex
// 1) Verify the Case service channel
SELECT Id, Name, DeveloperName
FROM ServiceChannel
ORDER BY Name
apex
// 2) Verify routing configurations
SELECT Id, Name, DeveloperName, RoutingPriority, IsActive
FROM RoutingConfig
ORDER BY RoutingPriority
apex
// 3) Verify presence statuses available to agents
SELECT Id, MasterLabel, DeveloperName, IsEnabled
FROM ServicePresenceStatus
ORDER BY MasterLabel
apex
// 4) Optional: skills-based routing â€” list skills assigned to cases
SELECT Id, Name, IsActive
FROM Skill
ORDER BY Name

Expected result: An agent who is in presence status Available receives a queued case as a popup work item within seconds of it being created. The supervisor can see the queue depth in the Omni-Channel Supervisor app, and idle work is redistributed when the routing config is enabled.

Common mistakes:

  • Expecting work items to appear when the agent lacks the Omni-Channel permission set or is not signed in to a console app â€” both are required.
  • Leaving an agent in Offline/Unavailable and wondering why no work pops.
  • Creating multiple routing configs without understanding order â€” the first matching config wins, so an aggressive config claims everything.
  • Routing work to a queue the agent is not a member of; the agent never sees the item.
  • Forgetting Omni-Channel only runs inside a Lightning console app, not a standard Lightning App.
14.4:
Approach: Entitlements model the SLA you owe a customer. An Entitlement definition (Entitlement Process) carries milestones â€” each milestone has a target deadline computed through business hours and, optionally, milestone time triggers with actions (field updates, email alerts, tasks) that fire before/after the target. Multiple Entitlement records hang off accounts/contacts, and cases link to one via Case.EntitlementId.

Setup:

  1. Setup â†’ Business Hours: create Support 9-5 for Monday to Friday.
  2. Setup â†’ Entitlement Definitions â†’ New Premium Support Process; attach the business hours.
  3. In Milestone Setup add milestone types Response and Resolution, each with a target in minutes/hours.
  4. Add milestone time triggers: e.g. Response at target â†’ Action: notify the case owner; Resolution 1 hour after target â†’ Action: assign to Tier 2 + set a custom Escalated__c boolean field. Add an Email Alert + Task as the action type.
  5. Create Entitlement records (AccountId, Name, Status = Active) and enable them on case record types.
apex
// 1) Verify active entitlement processes
SELECT Id, Name, IsActive, BusinessHoursId
FROM EntitlementProcess
ORDER BY LastModifiedDate DESC
apex
// 2) Verify the milestone items inside the process
SELECT Id, MilestoneTypeId, MilestoneType.Name
FROM EntitlementProcessMilestoneItem
WHERE SlaProcessId != null
ORDER BY MilestoneType.Name
apex
// 3) Verify time triggers on those milestones
SELECT Id, EntitlementProcessMilestoneItemId, TriggerOrder,
       OffsetUnit, OffsetAmount, Action, ActionType
FROM EntitlementProcessMilestoneTimeTrigger
ORDER BY TriggerOrder
apex
// 4) Show cases protected by an entitlement
SELECT Id, CaseNumber, Subject, Status, EntitlementId, Entitlement.Name
FROM Case
WHERE EntitlementId != null
ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC

Expected result: When a case is created against an active Entitlement, milestone rows (CaseMilestone) appear with computed TargetDate based on business hours. When a milestone is exceeded, the time-trigger action fires (escalation, email alert, field update), and the process shows active in the SOQL queries.

Common mistakes:

  • Confusing the definition (Entitlement Process) with the assignment (Entitlement record) â€” a case must reference an Entitlement, not the process directly.
  • Skipping Business Hours so targets compute against GMT calendar time instead of your support hours.
  • Forgetting that process edits create new versions; existing entitlements keep using the old version until reactivated/assigned to the new one.
  • Setting an action on the process but leaving the milestone time trigger off, so nothing fires at the boundary.
  • Not assigning an Entitlement to the Account/Contact record type used, so cases never pick up an SLA.
14.5:
Approach: SLA compliance = percentage of completion. Each milestone is a CaseMilestone row flagged IsViolated. SOQL has no CASE/WHEN, so compute met vs violated counts by grouping on IsViolated, then assemble the compliance matrix in Apex or in a report.

apex
// Raw aggregate: count completed milestones per milestone type, met vs violated
SELECT MilestoneTypeId, MilestoneType.Name, IsViolated, COUNT(Id) total
FROM CaseMilestone
WHERE CompletionDate != null
GROUP BY MilestoneTypeId, MilestoneType.Name, IsViolated
ORDER BY MilestoneType.Name
apex
// Apex service that turns the aggregate into a compliance percentage
public with sharing class SlaComplianceMatrix {

  public static Map<String, SlaRow> compute() {
    Map<String, SlaRow> rows = new Map<String, SlaRow>();
    for (AggregateResult ar : [
      SELECT MilestoneTypeId, IsViolated, COUNT(Id) total
      FROM CaseMilestone
      WHERE CompletionDate != null
      GROUP BY MilestoneTypeId, IsViolated
    ]) {
      String key = String.valueOf(ar.get('MilestoneTypeId'));
      SlaRow row = rows.containsKey(key) ? rows.get(key) : new SlaRow(key);
      Integer total = Integer.valueOf(ar.get('total'));
      if ((Boolean) ar.get('IsViolated') == true) row.violated += total;
      else row.met += total;
      rows.put(key, row);
    }
    return rows;
  }

  public class SlaRow {
    public final String milestoneTypeId;
    public Integer met = 0;
    public Integer violated = 0;
    public SlaRow(String milestoneTypeId) {
      this.milestoneTypeId = milestoneTypeId;
    }
    public Decimal compliancePct() {
      Integer total = met + violated;
      return total == 0 ? 0 : met * 100 / total;
    }
  }
}
apex
// Run from an anonymous window to see the numbers
Map<String, SlaComplianceMatrix.SlaRow> rows =
  SlaComplianceMatrix.compute();
for (String key : rows.keySet()) {
  SlaComplianceMatrix.SlaRow r = rows.get(key);
  System.debug(key + ' => met ' + r.met + ' / violated ' + r.violated
               + ' / compliance ' + r.compliancePct() + '%');
}

Expected result: The debug output lists each milestone type with met, violated, and compliance %. In a real org this becomes the SLA Compliance Report, and the numbers reconcile with the Case Milestones report type.

Common mistakes:

  • Trying to write SUM(CASE WHEN IsViolated = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) â€” SOQL does not support CASE expressions, so GROUP BY + Apex arithmetic is the correct pattern.
  • Forgetting the CompletionDate != null filter, which drags still-open milestones into the compliance math.
  • Casting AggregateResult values with (Integer) on COUNT â€” use Integer.valueOf(...) to avoid conversion errors.
  • Ignoring milestones whose MilestoneTypeId is null, which produces a misleading bucket.
14.6:
Approach: Violations live on CaseMilestone, not on Case. List the flagged rows joined to their case and milestone so the report shows which customers are missing their SLA, and use date filters to bound the window.

apex
// All violated milestones, newest first
SELECT Id, CaseId, Case.CaseNumber, Case.Subject, Case.Status,
       MilestoneTypeId, MilestoneType.Name,
       EntitlementId, Entitlement.Name,
       TargetDate, CompletionDate, IsViolated
FROM CaseMilestone
WHERE IsViolated = true
ORDER BY TargetDate DESC
apex
// Violations in the last 30 days only
SELECT Id, Case.CaseNumber, Case.Subject,
       MilestoneType.Name, TargetDate, CompletionDate, IsViolated
FROM CaseMilestone
WHERE IsViolated = true
  AND TargetDate >= LAST_N_DAYS:30
ORDER BY Case.CaseNumber, TargetDate
apex
// Count violations per owner, handy for a management dashboard
SELECT Case.Owner.Name, COUNT(Id) violations
FROM CaseMilestone
WHERE IsViolated = true
  AND TargetDate >= LAST_N_DAYS:30
GROUP BY Case.Owner.Name
ORDER BY COUNT(Id) DESC

Expected result: A list of every milestone that breached its target, with the case number, milestone name, the promised date (TargetDate) and the actual date (CompletionDate). The grouped query gives per-owner violation counts for the last 30 days.

Common mistakes:

  • Looking for the flag on the Case record â€” IsViolated exists only on CaseMilestone.
  • Recomputing the flag as CompletionDate > TargetDate when the platform already evaluated the deadline with business hours; use IsViolated to stay consistent with the SLA the customer sees.
  • Leaving out the date predicate and producing an unbounded, slow report.
  • Filtering on CompletionDate = null expecting violations â€” open milestones are separate from violated ones until an evaluation marks them.
14.7:
Approach: Data categories tag Knowledge articles so agents and customers can browse/filter by topic, region, or product. Categories live in a category group assigned to an article type; each article carries its selections on the Data Category Selection tab. SOQL can both inspect assignments and filter searches with the WITH DATA CATEGORY clause.

Setup:

  1. Setup â†’ Knowledge â†’ Data Categories: create a category group Region with children North America, EMEA, APAC.
  2. Attach the data category group to the FAQ article type (Article Types â†’ FAQ â†’ Data Categories).
  3. On an article record open the Data Category Selection tab and tick Region â†’ North America.
  4. Verify category that users can see with their profile via Data Category Visibility settings.
apex
// 1) Search published articles
SELECT Id, Title, KnowledgeArticleId, UrlName, PublishStatus,
       VersionNumber, IsLatestVersion
FROM KnowledgeArticleVersion
WHERE PublishStatus = 'Online'
  AND Language = 'en_US'
ORDER BY LastPublishedDate DESC
apex
// 2) See which categories an article is tagged with
Id articleId = 'ka0D0000000abcDCA'; // hold the KnowledgeArticleId
SELECT Id, DataCategoryName, ParentId
FROM DataCategorySelection
WHERE ParentId = :articleId
apex
// 3) Filter a search to one branch of the category tree
SELECT Id, Title, KnowledgeArticleId
FROM KnowledgeArticleVersion
WHERE PublishStatus = 'Online'
  WITH DATA CATEGORY Region__c ABOVE north_america

Expected result: Articles appear under the right category filters in the Service Console Knowledge tab, and the WITH DATA CATEGORY query returns only articles tagged in the North America branch. Step 2 lists the DataCategorySelection rows that back those tags.

Common mistakes:

  • Thinking Apex can insert DataCategorySelection â€” category assignment is done in the article UI/at publish time, not via DML.
  • Using the wrong operator: SOQL supports ABOVE, BELOW, AT, ABOVE_OR_BELOW(not valid), and EXCLUDE â€” WITH DATA CATEGORY Region__c ABOVE_OR_BELOW ... throws an error.
  • Typing the category label instead of the API suffix (Region__c) â€” the clause needs the suffixed name and the exact category key.
  • Forgetting PublishStatus = 'Online', which either errors or returns drafts nobody can use.
  • Assigning categories but leaving the data category group invisible to the agent profile, so the filter returns nothing.
14.8:
Approach: The Service Console is a Lightning console app: utility bar on the right, workspace tabs, navigation sidebar, and behavior tweaks like case feed style. Components such as Omni-Channel, macros, Notes, or custom Lightning Web Components plug into the utility bar or an app page.

Setup:

  1. App Manager â†’ Service Console â†’ App Settings â†’ enable Console (Lightning console) â€” this unlocks workspace tabs, the utility bar, and omni.
  2. Add utility items: Notes, Macros, Omni-Channel Supervisor, and a custom LWC you ship in the repo.
  3. Configure Case Feed style (Tab or Highlight Panel) and utilities such as click-to-dial (softphone).
  4. Give agents the console permissions (Omni-Channel, Macro authoring) through permission sets.

Common mistakes:

  • Editing a standard Lightning app and expecting console behavior â€” you must create/convert to a Lightning console app explicitly.
  • Adding LWC targets to the utility bar but never adding the utility definition in the app settings â€” the component stays invisible.
  • Forgetting permission sets, so the Omni-Channel utility renders as an error tile.

14.9:
Approach: Macros are replayable action sequences an agent launches from the case page to batch through busywork â€” closing a case becomes one click: field updates, feed posts, email sends, waits. Create macros in the Service Console UI; they are stored as Macro/MacroInstruction records and can be attached to buttons or the Macro utility.

Setup:

  1. Open a Case in the Service Console â†’ Macros panel â†’ New Macro â†’ name Close Case Standard.

  2. Add instructions in order:

    • Update Field: Status = Closed
    • Update Field: CaseReason = User Initiated
    • Post Case Feed: Closed via macro â€” thanks for your patience
    • (optional) Send Email: use the Closing email template to the contact
  3. Save, then attach the macro to a Quick Action Run Macro on the Case layout or keep it in the Macro utility.
  4. Grant the Author Macros permission via a permission set.
apex
// Macros are console-managed; verify their definition records if your org
// exposes the Macro objects to the running user
SELECT Id, Name, MacroType
FROM Macro
ORDER BY Name
apex
// Inspect the instruction steps that make up a macro
SELECT Id, MacroId, InstructionType, SequenceNumber, TargetName, TargetValue
FROM MacroInstruction
ORDER BY MacroId, SequenceNumber

Expected result: One click launches the sequence: the case is closed, reason stamped, and a feed post logged. Reopen shows the action history, and the macro appears in the Macro list for authorized agents.

Common mistakes:

  • Editing macros from the Developer Console â€” macros are edited in the Service Console macro editor, and Apex DML against MacroInstruction is not supported.
  • Leaving a macro with no terminating, field-changing/feed/send step, so the sequence ends without an observable action.
  • Missing permissions â€” agents without Macro authoring/console access never see the Macro tab.
  • Referencing layout labels in update instructions instead of the field API name, causing the step to No Whitelisted fail.
  • Attaching a macro to a chat flow where agent guidance is not applicable â€” macros are case/console-centric.
CAP:
Approach: The capstone wires everything the prior exercises built into one org: intake (email/web/chat), routing (queues + assignment rule + Omni-Channel), SLA (entitlement process with milestones + batch monitor), knowledge deflection, a console app, macros, and a compliance report. Below is the reference implementation â€” a lifecycle service that applies the account's entitlement before insert and triggers MultiChannelCaseRouter enrichment, plus the verification queries for the final deliverable.

apex
// CaseLifecycle.trigger
trigger CaseLifecycle on Case (before insert, before update) {
  CaseLifecycleService.applyEntitlement(Trigger.new);
}
apex
public with sharing class CaseLifecycleService {

  public static void applyEntitlement(List<Case> cases) {
    Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
    for (Case c : cases) if (c.AccountId != null) accountIds.add(c.AccountId);

    Map<Id, Entitlement> entitlementByAccount = new Map<Id, Entitlement>();
    for (Entitlement e : [
      SELECT Id, AccountId, Name, Status
      FROM Entitlement
      WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
        AND Status = 'Active'
      ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
    ]) {
      if (!entitlementByAccount.containsKey(e.AccountId)) {
        entitlementByAccount.put(e.AccountId, e);
      }
    }

    for (Case c : cases) {
      if (c.EntitlementId == null) {
        Entitlement e = entitlementByAccount.get(c.AccountId);
        if (e != null) c.EntitlementId = e.Id;
      }
    }
    MultiChannelCaseRouter.enrich(cases);
  }
}
apex
// Scheduled enforcement: reuse the MP2 monitor but tune its filters
public class CapstoneScheduler implements Schedulable {
  public void execute(SchedulableContext ctx) {
    Database.executeBatch(new SlaMonitorBatch(), 200);
    KnowledgeDeflectionService.findSuggestions('deflect', 1); // warm the search cache
  }
}
// Schedule it: System.schedule('CapstoneDaily', '0 0 3 * * ?', new CapstoneScheduler());

Final verification queries (paste each into the Developer Console):

apex

SELECT COUNT(Id) queued FROM GroupMember WHERE Group.Type = 'Queue';
SELECT COUNT(Id) violations FROM CaseMilestone WHERE IsViolated = true;
SELECT COUNT(Id) relatedArticles FROM CaseArticle;

Expected result: An agent in the Service Console opens a case that auto-arrived from email/chat, sees the SLA milestones ticking against business hours, runs the Quick Close macro, and the compliance report shows > 95% on-time â€” with knowledge articles absorbing the repeat questions first.

Common mistakes:

  • Wiring before insert enrichment that DMLs String/trigger recursion â€” guard with a static boolean or offload to a Flow invocation after insert.
  • Ignoring with sharing â€” the service must respect the running user's record visibility or escalation info leaks between orgs.
  • Deploying code and metadata without dependency order (queues before assignment rules, entitlement processes before Entitlements, batch + schedules last), which breaks the first install.
  • Shipping the LWC to a lightning__RecordPage with no lightning__UtilityBar target, and shipping the macro XML without the Macro author permission.
  • Treating the capstone as a single deliverable â€” concrete artifacts plus documented deployment should mirror exactly what the 14.1-14.9 exercises established.
MP1:
Approach: One case pipeline for every inbound channel: email (Email-to-Case), web (Web-to-Case), chat (Omni-Channel), and the API. Ingestion is declarative; the value-add is enrichment â€” dedupe by contact email, fill Account/Contact context, pick the queue, and let entitlement logic apply. The Apex service below is invoked from a Flow (or an apex-defined invocable action) after a case is inserted.

Setup:

  1. Setup â†’ Email-to-Case: enable org-wide, create support@acme.com, map to the Case record type, thread on SuppliedEmail/Subject.
  2. Setup â†’ Web-to-Case: create a form and generate the embed snippet for the website.
  3. Chat: enable Omni-Channel + the Case service channel (see 14.3).
  4. Create a Flow Case Intake Pipeline triggered on Case insert that calls the service below, then reassigns the owner to the matching queue.
apex
public with sharing class MultiChannelCaseRouter {

  public static final Id PREMIUM_QUEUE_ID = [
    SELECT Id FROM Group
    WHERE Type = 'Queue' AND DeveloperName = 'Premium_Support'
    LIMIT 1
  ].Id;

  // Invocable so a Flow can call it: enrich, then the flow routes
  @InvocableMethod(label='Route multi-channel cases')
  public static List<Id> route(List<List<Case>> inputs) {
    List<Case> cases = inputs[0];
    enrich(cases);
    for (Case c : cases) {
      if (c.Origin == 'Web' && c.Priority == 'High') {
        if (c.OwnerId == null) c.OwnerId = PREMIUM_QUEUE_ID;
      }
    }
    updatedCases(cases);
    return new List<Id>{ cases.isEmpty() ? null : cases[0].Id };
  }

  private static void enrich(List<Case> cases) {
    Set<String> emails = new Set<String>();
    for (Case c : cases) {
      if (!String.isBlank(c.SuppliedEmail)) {
        emails.add(c.SuppliedEmail.toLowerCase());
      }
    }
    Map<String, Contact> byEmail = new Map<String, Contact>();
    for (Contact con : [SELECT Id, AccountId, Email FROM Contact WHERE Email IN :emails]) {
      byEmail.put(con.Email.toLowerCase(), con);
    }
    for (Case c : cases) {
      if (!String.isBlank(c.SuppliedEmail)) {
        Contact matched = byEmail.get(c.SuppliedEmail.toLowerCase());
        if (matched != null) {
          c.ContactId = matched.Id;
          c.AccountId = matched.AccountId;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  private static void updatedCases(List<Case> cases) {
    // Outbound note: if called later in the flow, DML is owned by the Flow user.
    Database.update(cases, false);
  }
}
apex
// Auditing inbound email volume (# of email-originated cases today)
SELECT COUNT(Id) emails, COUNT_DISTINCT(FromAddress) senders
FROM EmailMessage
WHERE Incoming = true
  AND MessageDate >= TODAY
apex
// Sanity check: cases from every channel in the premium queue
SELECT Origin, COUNT(Id) n
FROM Case
WHERE OwnerId = :MultiChannelCaseRouter.PREMIUM_QUEUE_ID
  AND CreatedDate >= LAST_N_DAYS:7
GROUP BY Origin

Expected result: Cases arriving from email, web, and chat land in the shared queue with the correct Account/Contact lookup already resolved, and the weekly query shows a clean Origin breakdown.

Common mistakes:

  • Expecting Email-to-Case to dedupe automatically â€” it threads in a case but does not merge; pair it with Case Duplicate Rules or the enrichment above.
  • Setting OwnerId to a queue from Apex when the running user lacks Transfer Cases â€” the DML fails or the case flips to personal ownership.
  • Enrichment running after routing, so routing never sees the account/contact you just filled (order the Flow sub-steps correctly).
  • Using c.OwnerId == null guards carelessly â€” a half-routed case may already have an owner.
  • Forgetting the Origin mapping so every channel lumped into Phone breaks reporting.
MP2:
Approach: Entitlement milestones evaluate on save (see 14.4), but monitoring, alerting, and escalation of at-risk SLAs deserve a proactive background job. This batch flags overdue CaseMilestones and sends a Chatter post to the case owner â€” then a scheduler fires it every morning. Pair it with Business Hours math when you need a target computed mid-day.

apex
public with sharing class SlaMonitorBatch implements Database.Batchable<SObject> {

  public Database.QueryLocator start(Database.BatchableContext ctx) {
    return Database.getQueryLocator([
      SELECT Id, CaseId, Case.CaseNumber, Case.Owner.Email,
             MilestoneTypeId, MilestoneType.Name,
             TargetDate, CompletionDate, IsViolated,
             EntitlementId, Entitlement.Name
      FROM CaseMilestone
      WHERE CompletionDate = null
        AND TargetDate != null
        AND TargetDate < LAST_N_DAYS:1
      ORDER BY TargetDate ASC
    ]);
  }

  public void execute(Database.BatchableContext ctx, List<SObject> scope) {
    List<CaseMilestone> overdue = (List<CaseMilestone>) scope;
    List<FeedItem> posts = new List<FeedItem>();
    for (CaseMilestone cm : overdue) {
      System.debug('Overdue: Case ' + cm.Case.CaseNumber
                   + ' milestone ' + cm.MilestoneType.Name
                   + ' target ' + cm.TargetDate);
      posts.add(new FeedItem(
        ParentId = cm.CaseId,
        Body = 'SLA alert: ' + cm.MilestoneType.Name
             + ' was due when Customer did not close. Please respond.'
      ));
    }
    if (!posts.isEmpty()) insert posts;
  }

  public void finish(Database.BatchableContext ctx) {
    System.debug('SLA monitor finished. Job: ' + ctx.getJobId());
    // Optional: kick the next run or log to a custom object
  }
}

// Scheduler so the monitor runs at 4am UTC daily
public class SlaMonitorScheduler implements Schedulable {
  public void execute(SchedulableContext ctx) {
    Database.executeBatch(new SlaMonitorBatch(), 200);
  }
}

// Business hours aware target computation (used when building milestones)
BusinessHours bh = [SELECT Id FROM BusinessHours WHERE IsDefault = true LIMIT 1];
DateTime target = BusinessHours.add(
  bh.Id, DateTime.now(), 4L * 60 * 60 * 1000  // +4 business hours (ms)
);

Expected result: At 4am the job runs: overdue milestones are logged, owners get a Chatter alert on the related case, and the AsyncApexJob query confirms the runs with their processed item counts.

Common mistakes:

  • Misusing the cron format â€” System.schedule needs the flowing 7-field 0 0 4 * * ? seconds-first format; a 5-field crontab string throws.
  • SQL with unbounded scope: forgetting CompletionDate = null so every historical milestone gets re-flagged.
  • Querying in a loop inside execute â€” use the scope; governor limits are real.
  • Treating BusinessHours.add intervals as hours â€” the third argument is milliseconds, so convert hours 60 60 * 1000.
  • Scheduling more jobs than the platform allows (max 100 queued batches) and hitting System.LimitException on executeBatch.
